newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian avg money market rate eases to 10.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian avg money market rate eases to 10.6 pct.

text.p: Croatia's average money market rate eased back to 10.6 percent on Wednesday from 11.2 percent after lenders reduced term placements amid a shortage of funds.
Of 42.9 million kuna total trade, 20 million were rolled over old loans. Demand totalled 45 million kuna.
Interbank rates were firm at call money and seven-day price of 10 percent, and 12-15 percent for eight- to 30-day kuna.
Savings banks paid a higher 17 percent for one- and 18 percent for two-month kuna.
Insurers renewed 7.5 million kuna in seven-day deals at an unchanged nine percent.
To ease liquidity strains, the National Bank of Croatia today bought a large amount of German marks from the banking sector. It will pay kuna to banks on Friday.

Its kuna midrates for Thursday were calculated a touch firmer at 6.1569 to the dollar, but weaker at 3.5688 against the mark after the intervention. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
